summary.name: Stedding Browser
summary.one_liner: An open-source, Arc-style desktop browser built on Chromium, with a vertical-tab sidebar, Spaces, pinned tabs, a command bar and one-click import from Arc.
use_cases: organise work and personal browsing into separate Spaces
keep separate sign-ins for one site in different Spaces
browse privately without telemetry or an account
sync browser sidebar across Macs and Windows PCs through a cloud folder
migrate Arc, Safari, Dia or Firefox data into a new browser
summary.what_it_does: Stedding is a desktop browser built on Chromium stable that reproduces Arc's sidebar-based workflow: vertical tabs, Spaces with their own colour and icon, folders, and pinned tabs that return to their home page. A command bar (Command T / Ctrl+T) searches, opens URLs, and jumps to any open or archived tab. Spaces can optionally use an independent session with separate cookies while sharing extensions and settings, and split view, a hideable sidebar, and dark-page switching are included. It can import Arc's Spaces, tabs, history and passwords in one step, and syncs the sidebar through a user-chosen folder such as iCloud Drive or Dropbox rather than a company server. Extensions install from the Chrome Web Store, and built-in ad and tracker blocking is off until enabled.
notable: Open source under BSD-3-Clause with no account required
Spaces can keep independent sign-ins within one profile
One-click import of Arc data, plus Safari, Dia and Firefox
Sidebar sync through a user-chosen cloud folder with no server
caveats: Early beta (0.4.0 beta 1); Windows installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen warns once
Intel Macs and Linux are not supported yet
Safe Browsing is not active, and Netflix, Disney+ and Spotify need Widevine, which is not yet available
Chrome, Brave and the new Edge cannot be imported yet
